heroHeadline: Day 89 of Op Ghazab — UN OHCHR Warns Afghan Deportees Face Persecution Risk; 20-Day Strike Pause Holds; Journalists Day 16–19 in Taliban Detention
heroSubtitle: On May 25, 2026 (Day 89 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) warned through spokesperson Shabia Mantoo that forced returns to Afghanistan expose deportees to 'serious risks of persecution, abuse and other human rights violations' — directly challenging Pakistan's mass deportation campaign that has expelled over 146,000 Afghans in 2026. The 20-day pause in confirmed Pakistani cross-border airstrikes into Afghanistan since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike continues to hold, with Pakistan maintaining its precision intelligence-based operations (IBOs) within Pakistani territory. The IBO campaign through May has killed: 22+ militants in Shewa sanitization (May 17-20), Afghan commander Basir in Arjam Kali (May 20), 4 including wanted commander Tor Saqib in Spinwam (May 21), 11 in Datta Khel (May 24 — internationally confirmed by Xinhua on May 25). Three journalists remain in Taliban General Directorate of Intelligence custody: Paigard News Agency head Jawid Niazi (Day 19 — detained May 6), TOLO News presenter Mansoor Niazi (Day 18 — detained May 7), and TOLO News political editor Imran Danish (Day 16 — detained May 9). The Taliban announced intent to put the TOLOnews journalists on trial; no charges have been formally filed. UNAMA's May 22 formal 'grave concern' over Taliban Decree No. 18 — which treats a girl's silence as consent to marriage — remains unanswered. OCHA's May 2026 Contingency Plan documents compounding displacement scenarios from the Af-Pak conflict and Iran-related returnee pressure. No formal ceasefire; no Urumqi Round 2 date; China has been silent on mediation since April 8.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA, Express Tribune, Pakistan Today, ISPR, Xinhua, CPJ, Amnesty International
